title: POC workload delta, concurrency & token dynamics scoping - Veritide
next_steps: Redwood to share the benchmark template and sample playback harness by 2027-09-09
Veritide to export 2 weeks of traffic samples (anonymized) and a 24h tail window by 2027-09-13
Schedule 2-hour deep dive for token distribution replay and kernel-level profiling week of 2027-09-20
action_items: Ava: send benchmark template + list of required logs by 2027-09-09
Marcus: prepare initial throughput map and recommended concurrency ladder by 2027-09-10
Jonas: share sanitized request/response samples and current token histograms by 2027-09-13

summary: Discovery/POC scoping focused on characterizing Veritide's QPS bursts, concurrency distribution, and input/output token mix. Discussed goals for tail-latency SLOs, benchmark methodology (replay vs synthetic), required artifacts, and timeline for a 3-week pilot. Key concerns: data residency, on-prem option for regulated workloads, and ability to reproduce production burst patterns for kernel-level profiling.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment considerations
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-07 15:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Veritide Head of Platform), Jonas Meyer (ML Eng), Leah Kim (SRE)

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: hey all, Priya here, head of platform at Veritide, we're exploring a pilot to move our conversational assistant inference off our homegrown stack into something more predictable for cost and latency.
[00:18] Jonas: Jonas, ML eng, I'll be owning the traffic samples and running the initial replays.
[00:23] Leah: Leah, SRE, I'll be looking at tail latency and availability requirements.
[00:29] Ava: great. Marcus is our systems SE, he'll lead on workload mapping and the benchmark config. Marcus?
[00:36] Marcus (Redwood SE): hey, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) understand your traffic shape: QPS, concurrency, token distributions; 2) success criteria for the POC; 3) artifacts we need to run representative benchmarks; 4) timeline and next steps.

[02:12] Priya: high level — our assistant supports interactive and async flows. Baseline qps is low-ish, 1-3 rps avg, but we get spiky bursts during support hours and marketing campaigns, those spikes can hit 250-300 QPS for a few minutes. We're really worried about tails, like p99 and p999.

[03:05] Marcus: got it. can you clarify concurrency vs qps for us? are those 250 QPS sustained or ephemeral?

[03:12] Jonas: ephemeral — more like shot noise. The concurrency map is skewed: most requests are single-turn short prompts but 10% are multi-turn contexts with large input tokens (user message + context).

[03:28] Leah: also note we have a batch job that kicks off every 4 hours which causes a medium-length throughput burst for embeddings generation — that one is predictable.

[04:00] Ava: perfect, that's useful. For the POC we usually build two workload profiles: 1) interactive short-turn with high QPS spikes, and 2) long-turn conversations with heavier output tokens but lower QPS. Which of these is highest priority?

[04:18] Priya: short-turn spikes are our immediate pain. If you can show tail latency under 300ms p99 for the short-turns at our peak, we can move forward. The long-turns are important for cost analysis.

[05:02] Marcus: 300ms p99 — okay that's tight but doable depending on model and hardware. Are you currently using an open model quantized onboard or a hosted model?

[05:12] Jonas: currently self-hosted on mixed GPUs, using a 7B-ish model with int8 quantization. But we haven't tuned batching or KV cache management; we see weird tokenization spikes that blow up output token counts sometimes.

[05:28] Ava: that tokenization spike — do you have token histograms or average input/output token lengths?

[05:33] Jonas: I've got a couple of dumps. median input tokens ~18, median output ~24, but tail at 95th is input 120, output 600 for some multi-turn sessions.

[06:02] Marcus: nice, those numbers are exactly what we need. For sizing we use a mixture model: a 70/30 split short/long, then we overlay burst multipliers. Can you confirm the typical concurrency per user session? like do you send multiple parallel requests per user?

[06:22] Priya: generally single-threaded per session, but ops workflows trigger parallel calls for reranking+summaries sometimes — that's about 5% of traffic.

[07:10] Ava: ok. On the benchmark methodology: Marcus, can you outline the recommended playback approach?

[07:18] Marcus: yeah. Two-phase: 1) Replay phase where we use sanitized production logs to replay exact arrival times and token lengths into our harness; 2) Stress-phase where we synthetically amplify burst patterns to test autoscaling and tail behaviors. For kernel-level profiling we may need a dedicated run with constant sequence lengths so we can instrument kv cache, attention kernels etc.

[07:56] Leah: when you say replay, are you using exact timestamps and inter-arrival times? we need to be sure you can reproduce sub-second bursts.

[08:05] Marcus: yes, we capture inter-arrival deltas and preserve them in the playback harness. small caveat: we anonymize payloads and scrub PII before ingestion.

[08:22] Jonas: how do you handle tokens for reranking flows? that's more than one model call per request.

[08:30] Marcus: good question. we'll model multi-call flows as chained requests — we can parameterize time between calls, and the benchmark will respect per-request KV caches where appropriate. if you use separate reranker models, we model those endpoints separately.

[09:00] Priya: security question — we need to know about on-prem/private options. Some customers require data never leave our VPC. Can Redwood run in our VPC with KMS integration?

[09:12] Ava: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and HSM/KMS integrations and audit logs. For the POC we can either run against our hosted infra or spin a private deployment in your cloud region. There are timeline tradeoffs.

[09:38] Leah: timeline tradeoffs meaning setup time? how long to stand up a private control plane?

[09:44] Ava: private is typically 3-4 weeks for enterprise onboarding, hosted trial with benchmark replay we can do in 1-2 weeks. For the POC we usually recommend hosted first to validate performance shape, then migrate to private later if needed.

[10:12] Jonas: given our compliance we might have to do private, but yeah we can start hosted for profiling if you can guarantee logs and no persisted data.

[10:24] Marcus: we'll provide a benchmark harness that can run against either endpoint. For accurate tail analysis we recommend you provide at least two weeks of traffic and a focused 24-hour window that captured a representative campaign spike.

[11:05] Priya: ok we'll pull that. On success criteria — besides 300ms p99 for short-turns, we want p99.9 tail under 600ms for critical flows and a cost-per-1000 token target that's better than our current baseline. Also key is no more than 0.5% error/regression in generation quality.

[11:35] Ava: quality gating — do you have a set of eval prompts?

[11:40] Jonas: we have a 150 prompt eval set with graded metrics. We'll share that.

[12:00] Marcus: excellent. For cost comparison we'll run throughput-to-cost curves: different batching configs, quantization levels, and model variants. That will give you a tradeoff table.

[12:18] Leah: curious about autoscaling — do you do fast scale-up for spikes? we can't risk cold-start failures.

[12:25] Marcus: Redwood's dedicated pools can autoscale with burst capacity; for hosted we have warm standby and model variant fallback rules to gracefully degrade rather than fail. But to prove it we should simulate 3x burst in the stress phase.

[13:02] Priya: can we get logs for every token timing? we want to see where time is spent — decode vs network vs server scheduling.

[13:10] Marcus: absolutely. Our benchmark exports token-level timing, per-request breakdowns, and trace ids so you can map to your observability. note sometimes transcriber logs mislabel KV cache as K-V catch in our records — just FYI, you'll see some inconsistencies in older dumps.

[13:40] Jonas: haha yes we've seen the 'K-V catch' typo. Noted.

[14:05] Ava: okay, let's go through the concrete artifacts we need: 1) sanitized request logs with timestamps and token counts; 2) model metadata (current model family, quantization); 3) your eval set; 4) security contact for the questionnaire. Anything else?

[14:22] Priya: also the rerank flow traces and any examples where outputs blow up token counts.

[14:32] Jonas: and the embedding batch schedule, since that implicates capacity.

[14:38] Marcus: great. On sizing: with your numbers (median in 18, median out 24, 95th in 120, 95th out 600) and a 70/30 short/long split, initial capacity estimate is a small dedicated pool for validation, but if you want p99 300ms at 250QPS spikes we'll probably need to test model variants; a smaller quantized model on faster GPUs might hit the SLO for short-turns.

[15:10] Jonas: so you'll recommend model swaps and batching config?

[15:14] Marcus: yes — we'll provide recommended concurrency ladder and batching windows. Also, be prepared for tokenization outliers: sometimes a single request expands to multiple KBs of tokens due to poor tokenization — we flag those for prefiltering.

[15:48] Leah: for the dedicated path, what telemetry do we get? I need per-token billing and per-route latency.

[15:56] Ava: Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and trace hooks. We can grant short-lived access for the POC.

[16:12] Priya: ok. On change windows — our ops wants to limit test impact. Can your replay harness run in a staging mirror rather than production?

[16:20] Marcus: yes, we run against a staging endpoint or a separate namespace to avoid production interference.

[16:32] Jonas: let's talk about the benchmark schedule. If you can deliver the harness by 2027-09-09, and we provide logs by 2027-09-13, how long until results?

[16:41] Marcus: typical turnaround is 3 working days for the first replay run, then 3 days for stress-phase and tuning. So about two weeks end-to-end for meaningful results.

[16:54] Ava: so that aligns with a 3-week pilot timeline. Does that timeline work for you?

[17:02] Priya: yes, that's acceptable. One more thing — we need an escape hatch if the hosted results show data residency issues. How quickly can you replicate the benchmark in a private deployment?

[17:12] Ava: standing up private for benchmarking usually adds 2-3 weeks. We can include that as a contingency.

[17:30] Jonas: for the replay, is there a required format? CSV/JSON?

[17:35] Marcus: JSONL with fields: timestamp, request_id, model_endpoint, input_token_count, output_token_count (optional for generated), and optionally chained_calls array. We'll annotate the schema in the template we send.

[17:58] Priya: about quality gating — if there's a 0.5% degradation we need rollback. How do you measure semantic regressions?

[18:06] Marcus: we run your eval set through both systems and compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics plus a human-grade sample. We'll keep the same seed and sampling parameters. If you use proprietary eval metrics, we can plug them in.

[18:40] Leah: request for observability — include per-request resource usage and per-GPU queue depth. those are crucial for our SRE playbooks.

[18:52] Marcus: we export queue depth, kernel utilization, and per-token time breakdown when running on dedicated hardware. For hosted tests some low-level kernel hooks may be approximated unless we run on dedicated hardware with profiling enabled.

[19:18] Priya: hmm, kernel-level profiling may be required for our internal approval.

[19:25] Ava: then we should plan a dedicated run with profiling enabled — that would fit into week 2 of the pilot.

[19:39] Jonas: fine. Anything else on security? SSO and RBAC?

[19:44] Ava: Redwood supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC for consoles, plus audit logs retained per your retention policy in Private. We'll include the security questionnaire and SOC2 report.

[20:05] Leah: please add the contact for compliance.

[20:09] Ava: will do.

[20:20] Ava: let's recap next steps quickly. I'll send the benchmark template and harness link by Friday, Marcus will attach the sizing doc and recommended concurrency ladder, Jonas will provide logs and eval set by Monday next week, Leah will confirm security owner. We schedule a 2-hour deep dive for week of 2027-09-20 for token distribution replay.

[20:41] Jonas: sounds good. Quick clarifying Q: for multi-call reranking flows that have an internal delay, do you preserve inter-call latency?

[20:50] Marcus: yes we model the delay; it's parameterizable.

[21:02] Priya: any recommended prefilters to drop pathological tokenization cases?

[21:07] Marcus: we suggest a prefilter threshold at 5k tokens total — those will be routed to an async pipeline or truncated after human review. We'll document tradeoffs.

[21:22] Leah: we'll need the exact gating thresholds spelled out for our change plan.

[21:27] Ava: noted.

[21:36] Priya: okay that's it from me, thanks everyone.
[21:40] Ava: thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[21:45] Marcus: thanks all.

[21:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quirks: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'K-V catch' instead of KV cache), speaker overlaps, and truncated punctuation typical of automated transcripts. The technical sections included explicit QPS and token histograms (median and 95th percentiles), discussion of replay harness and profiling, and a clear set of next steps and action items.
